dedupe_keys.name: delft3d flexible mesh delft3d fm and delft3d 4 simulation engines

description: Delft3D Flexible Mesh (Delft3D FM) is the hydrodynamic modelling suite of Deltares, the Dutch water research institute, whose simulation engines (together with the older Delft3D 4 engines) are published as open source code on GitHub. The engines cover hydrodynamics on unstructured meshes (D-Flow FM), hydrology (D-Hydrology), real-time control of structures such as weirs, pumps and gates (D-Real Time Control), morphodynamics (D-Morphology), waves (D-Waves) and water quality with the DELWAQ kernel, for coastal, estuarine, river, rural and urban applications. The community portal reports 40,000 plus members, 447 key partners in 49 countries and more than 16,000 publications using Delft3D, so it is one of the most widely used hydraulic modelling systems for rivers, deltas and coasts. Most engines are licensed AGPL-3.0 or GPL-3.0, with utility libraries under LGPL-2.1; users can compile the kernels themselves, download a precompiled open source GUI after registering, or buy service packages for the validated precompiled suite, whose latest release is 2026.01 (November 2025). Caveats: model building and calibration need experienced modellers, the open source GUI has licence-check issues reported on the forum, large 3D runs need high-performance computing, and GitHub metadata could not be read from our environment. Simulation uses: river and urban flood inundation, levee and dike breach scenarios, storm surge, reservoir and irrigation canal operation with real-time control, sediment impacts on waterways and ports, and receiving-water quality downstream of wastewater discharges. Related records: TELEMAC-MASCARET (model-telemac-mascaret) and HEC-RAS (model-hec-ras) are alternatives, XBeach (model-xbeach) handles storm impacts on sandy coasts, and Delft-FEWS (platform-delft-fews) runs Delft3D models in operational forecasting.
